exposure: excessive obstetric interventions (induced labor, caesarean sections)
public policies to reduce obstetric interventions
outcome: trends in gestational age (GA) at birth
proportion of live births by GA (preterm, early term, 39-40 weeks)
cohort: The study analyzed 1,525,759 live births recorded in Sao Paulo city, Brazil, using data from Brazil's national live births information system (SINASC).
finding: The study found a right shift in the gestational age curve in Sao Paulo city between 2012 and 2019, with an increase in births at 39-40 weeks and a significant reduction in preterm (< 37 weeks) and early term (37-38 weeks) births.
mod_finding: The observed trends in gestational age at birth were consistent across different types of delivery, reflecting the impact of public policies aimed at reducing obstetric interventions such as induced labor and caesarean section.
cross-section timing: Data were collected annually between 2012 and 2019.
gest_age: Preterm (< 37 weeks), early term (37-38 weeks), 39 weeks, 40 weeks, and other gestational ages.
